transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-09-10
- Time: 14:00 ET (52 minutes)
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Casey (Redwood SE), Morgan (Redwood Eng), Ravi (SentraPay CTO), Elena (SentraPay ML), David (SentraPay SRE), Priya (SentraPay PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Quick review of weekly POC metrics: latency medians, p95, token cost.
- Discussed model sweep results between v1.2 (quantized), v1.3 (FP16 tuned), and v1.4 (latest weights).
- Agreed on forced-pinning plan for the production route with a shadow run of v1.4 for 24h.
- Identified rollback/emergency cutoff triggers and owner responsibilities.

Topics covered:
- model selection / catalog comparisons
- version pinning and soft-fallbacks
- emergency cutoff & tabletop drill
- perf anomalies (kv cache thrashing, cold start variance)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll go quickly, we've got about 50 minutes, want to review the sweep, results, and then the safety net run and cutover plan.
[00:18] Ravi Menon: sounds good, we've got Elena and David with context, we're mostly focused on throughput and any quality regressions.
[00:26] Casey Nguyen: quick note, we ran three configurations this week - v1.2-quant (6-bit), v1.3-fp16 (baseline tuned kernels), and v1.4-candidate (larger weights, improved instruction tuning). We measured median RT, p95, token cost per 1k, and hallucination rate on the dev prompt set.
[00:42] Elena Suarez: yeah the headline is: v1.3 gave us the best balance, median dropped 18% vs v1.2, cost delta ~+6% vs v1.2, quality roughly equivalent. v1.4 improved some edge-case factuality but p95 spiked, likely due to kv cache pressure on longer sessions.
[01:03] David Park: when you say kv cache pressure, are you seeing GC or thrash? we noticed memory noise on node 7 during the run.
[01:10] Morgan Li: our trace shows higher cache evictions for v1.4 at sequences > 1200 tokens, yes eviction churn causes re-computation and spikes. also the kernel selection falls back to slower path intermittently.
[01:25] Priya Rao: for our users, p95 is a hard requirement <600ms, so spikes are concerning. Our success criteria: p95 <600ms and <0.5% major hallucinations on the evaluation set.
[01:36] Jordan Patel: right - so proposal: force-pin production traffic to v1.3 for the next pilot window, while shadowing v1.4 on 100% of requests for 24 hours (no user-visible responses). If shadow shows stable p95 and no regression in hallucination, we consider a phased roll.
[01:54] Ravi Menon: shadowing 100% is heavy, does Redwood stream-line the cost estimate? we need the per-token delta.
[02:02] Casey Nguyen: yes, we already compiled a delta sheet - rough estimate: v1.4 token cost +18% vs v1.3 on average; but if p95 improves after kernel changes it might justify. link posted: https://redwood.link/poc/sentra/benchmarks (short link).
[02:18] Elena Suarez: One more thing - we care about deterministic failures: if any request for a given prompt fails due to OOM or timeouts, what's the immediate fallback?
[02:27] Jordan Patel: plan is immediate soft-fallback to v1.3 (pinned) with a circuit-breaker: 5% error rate over a 5m window triggers the emergency cutoff. We log a rollback event and page the oncall.
[02:40] David Park: who gets paged? our SRE or Redwood oncall?
[02:44] Jordan Patel: primary is SentraPay SRE (you) then Redwood SE oncall copy. We'll configure the webhook in the pilot to call your incident manager and post to the (shared) slack channel.
[02:55] Priya Rao: can we define the precise triggers, e.g., p95 >1200ms for 3 consecutive five-minute windows or error rate >5%?
[03:03] Casey Nguyen: yes. proposed triggers captured in the spreadsheet; I'll paste the line items to the drive. (brief typing) okay - triggers: p95 >1200ms for 3 windows OR 5xx rate >3% for 5m OR hallucination metric (human review alerts) >0.5% for a sample slice. Any of those will flip the emergency cutoff.
[03:28] Elena Suarez: that hallucination metric depends on human review - how fast is that pipeline?
[03:33] Morgan Li: we can run automated heuristics (named-entity mismatch) for a fast signal, then human QA within 2-4 hours for confirmation. The circuit-breaker will not wait on human QA, it will use the automated signal first.
[03:47] Ravi Menon: makes sense. What about warm vs cold starts? we saw a 400ms penalty on first token for v1.4 sometimes.
[03:54] Casey Nguyen: yes cold-start variance is higher on v1.4 because kernel path sometimes loads alternate GPU kernels. We recommend keeping a small warm pool pinned to v1.3 to meet the SLA, while letting Redwood autoscale for bursts.
[04:08] David Park: for Dedicated vs Hosted, this is still hosted pilot right? we want Dedicated later but currently can't commit the infra.
[04:14] Jordan Patel: correct, Hosted pilot. If you move to Dedicated we'll help pin kernels and reduce cold variance, but that's a later phase.
[04:22] Priya Rao: on rollbacks: we'd like a dry-run tabletop this week to ensure ops knows steps. can Redwood lead that?
[04:28] Jordan Patel: yep we'll lead the drill. proposed time Tue 09/16 at 10am ET.
[04:32] Elena Suarez: about the sample prompts, we updated the prompt set to include payment flows and edge errors - I uploaded the new testset to the shared folder.
[04:38] Casey Nguyen: got it. we'll ensure the same seed and randomization for the sweep to keep comparability. mention: we saw v1.2 quant artifacting on dates/amounts in 0.3% of cases - that was fixed in v1.3.
[04:52] Ravi Menon: is there any config we can flip to reduce the p95 on v1.4 short-term? small knob?
[04:59] Morgan Li: two knobs: reduce kv cache retention (tradeoff with long context coherency) or increase smaller batching windows - both reduce memory churn. But those change quality slightly; must test.
[05:12] Priya Rao: quality tradeoffs are sensitive for billing UX. prefer fallback to v1.3 until v1.4 stabilizes.
[05:18] Jordan Patel: consensus seems to be pin to v1.3, shadow v1.4 24h, run longer stress (24h) and then tabletop drill. We'll capture exact rollback steps and who clicks what.
[05:29] David Park: for logging, can we get token-level traces for the shadow runs?
[05:32] Casey Nguyen: yes, we can enable detailed traces for the shadow job; note this increases log volume and retention pricing - we'll share options.
[05:39] Elena Suarez: please also include an export of misprediction examples for manual triage.
[05:43] Jordan Patel: noted.
[05:45] Ravi Menon: any security/compliance blockers? we need KMS or HSM for key storage and per-route retention config to match our policy.
[05:53] Jordan Patel: Redwood supports KMS integrations and per-route retention. I'll send the SOC2 snapshot, and Morgan will include retention options in the follow-up doc.
[06:01] Morgan Li: small followup: if you plan dedicated later we can tune quant kernels to reduce the p95 gap. But for this pilot, pinned v1.3 + shadow + drill is low risk.
[06:11] Priya Rao: ok let's capture next steps and owners.
[06:16] Jordan Patel: quick recap: 1) Pin production route to v1.3 (Jordan) 2) Launch 24h shadow run of v1.4 at 100% shadow (Casey + Morgan) 3) Run 24h stress test with quantized variant to measure cost (Casey) 4) Tabletop rollback drill Tue 09/16 (Jordan leads) 5) Share benchmarks + triggers (Jordan) 6) SentraPay to confirm peak qps and retention policy (David + Priya)
[06:43] Elena Suarez: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[06:46] Jordan Patel: thanks team, will send minutes + links, reach out if anything else.

End of transcript.
